title: 502s after a 'harmless' framework upgrade (ALB health checks)
intro: After upgrading the web framework, the site returns 502 Bad Gateway. The instances are running, the app starts fine, and 'curl localhost:8080' on a box works. The Auto Scaling group keeps launching and terminating instances.

steps.prompt: Check target health for the web-tg target group (arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:111122223333:targetgroup/web-tg/6d0ecf831eec9f09).
steps.fake_output:
Target                Port  State      Reason                       Description
i-0a9b8c7d6e5f40312   8080  unhealthy  Target.ResponseCodeMismatch  Health checks failed with these codes: [404]
i-0b8c7d6e5f4031209   8080  unhealthy  Target.ResponseCodeMismatch  Health checks failed with these codes: [404]
steps.hint: The Description field shows the actual HTTP code the health check got.

steps.prompt: Every target returns 404 to the health check, so the ALB has nowhere to send traffic, hence the 502s. Read the health-check configuration of web-tg (same ARN).
steps.fake_output:
HealthCheckProtocol: HTTP
HealthCheckPort: traffic-port
HealthCheckPath: /health
Matcher: {"HttpCode": "200"}

steps.prompt: Check what the app now serves, from an instance: open a Session Manager session on i-0a9b8c7d6e5f40312.
steps.fake_output:
Starting session with SessionId: alice-0d9e8f7a6b5c4d3e2
sh-5.2$

steps.prompt: Inside the session, ask the app for /health and for the framework's new default health endpoint /healthz, printing just the status code of each with curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}'. Start with /health.
steps.hint: -o /dev/null discards the body; -w '%{http_code}' prints only the status.

steps.prompt: The upgrade moved the endpoint to /healthz. Point web-tg's health check at /healthz (same ARN) to stop the outage now; restoring /health in the app can follow in a normal deploy.
steps.fake_output:
HealthCheckPath: /healthz
(targets turn healthy after 3 consecutive successful checks, about 30 seconds)

steps.prompt: Confirm the ASG stopped churning: check web-asg's recent scaling activities.
steps.fake_output:
StartTime             Status      Description
2026-09-28T15:02:10Z  Successful  Terminating EC2 instance: i-0c7d6e5f403120987 (ELB health check failed)
2026-09-28T14:58:44Z  Successful  Launching a new EC2 instance: i-0b8c7d6e5f4031209
(no activity since 15:02: the group is stable)

resolution: The app worked perfectly; only its health endpoint moved. The framework upgrade changed the default route from /health to /healthz, so every health check got a 404, every target was marked unhealthy, and the ALB returned 502 because it had no healthy targets. The ASG made it look like instability: with ELB health checks, it terminated each 'unhealthy' instance and launched a replacement that failed the same way, in an endless loop. 'curl localhost:8080' worked because it tested the root path, not the health path. Checking the Reason field on target health turns a vague outage into a one-line diagnosis. Prevention: treat the health-check path as an API contract (a test that fails if it moves), and roll out upgrades with a canary instance that must pass ALB health checks before the rest are replaced.
